subject: Social Science
central_question: How do money, banks and different credit arrangements enable exchange and development, and why must affordable credit be made accessible to all?
in_scope_units: Money as a Medium of Exchange: barter and double coincidence of wants
Modern Forms of Money: currency, deposits and cheque payments
Loan Activities of Banks: deposits, reserves, borrowers and bank income
Two Different Credit Situations: productive credit and debt trap
Terms of Credit: interest, collateral, documentation and repayment
Variety of Credit Arrangements: village lenders, borrowers and cooperatives
Formal Sector Credit in India: RBI supervision and formal–informal differences
Formal and Informal Credit — Who Gets What?: unequal access
Self-Help Groups for the Poor: savings, group loans and bank linkage
Grameen Bank of Bangladesh and chapter summing up

known_pitfalls.claim: Money is needed only when goods are bought with cash.
known_pitfalls.correction: Money includes currency and demand deposits, and payments can be settled through cheques without cash.

known_pitfalls.claim: Credit always improves the borrower's condition.
known_pitfalls.correction: Credit can increase earnings or create a debt trap depending on risk, terms and repayment capacity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Interest rate is the only term of credit.
known_pitfalls.correction: Terms of credit include interest, collateral, documentation and the mode of repayment.

known_pitfalls.claim: Poor households depend on informal credit because it is cheaper.
known_pitfalls.correction: Informal credit is often costlier; poor households may depend on it because formal loans require access, documents and collateral.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with the NCERT shoe-manufacturer barter example.
Use the NCERT M. Salim cheque-payment example to explain demand deposits.
Compare the NCERT Salim and Swapna credit situations.
Use Megha's house loan and the Sonpur village cases to analyse terms of credit.
Conclude with the NCERT SHG and Grameen Bank examples.
